findings.title: Device ID is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, allowing rejected devices to bypass the limit on retry
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called on line 87 before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93. When `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is reached and `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the new device's key remains in `localCache` for the 29-minute TTL. On any subsequent request from the same device, `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache on line 83 and returns `nil`, allowing `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed and completely bypassing the device limit after the first failed request. Move `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` to after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

findings.title: wire_gen.go was not regenerated after changing ProvideAnonymousDeviceService and ProvideAnonDBStore signatures
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go` changed its parameter from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `ProvideAnonDBStore` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` added a `deviceLimit int64` parameter, but `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` (and any wire provider sets) was not updated in this PR. The server build will fail until Wire is re-run.

findings.title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 when UPDATE matches a row without changing values, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached
findings.body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is used to determine whether the device existed within the active window, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `rowsAffected == 0`. On MySQL (unless `clientFoundRows` is enabled on the DSN), `RowsAffected()` returns the number of rows actually modified rather than matched. If two requests for an existing device occur within the same second (MySQL's default timestamp precision, or when `updated_at`, `client_ip`, and `user_agent` are identical), `RowsAffected()` will be 0 even though the device row exists and matched the `WHERE` clause, falsely rejecting an already-registered device with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.
